title: Pipedrive Pricing Plans and Total Costs for 2026
summary: Pipedrive pricing structures for 2026 help you determine which subscription tier provides the necessary features to support your specific sales volume.
body_markdown:
## Pipedrive Pricing Plans and Feature Tiers


When the 2026 pricing model takes effect, your monthly overhead depends on the volume of automated actions your team triggers. The interface remains intuitive, but the transition from a tool that manages data to one that executes tasks carries a price multiplier.


### Essential: The Entry-Level CRM Pipeline


At $14 per seat monthly when billed annually, the Lite plan functions as a digital filing cabinet, which means users pay a recurring fee for basic storage rather than active sales tools. It lacks the automation engine entirely.


Because of this restriction, a growing team must manually update every stage change or contact detail.


This tier functions as a single source of truth for small operations that have more time than capital. By choosing this manual system, the team accepts the administrative burden of repetitive data entry.


### Advanced: Adding Workflow Automation and Email Sync


Stepping up to the Growth tier at $39 per seat introduces the first cap on efficiency, so your workflow will inevitably hit a wall as your team grows. Only **30 active automations** are permitted at this level.


When a sales manager hits this limit, they must choose which 30 sequences are vital enough to run.


To avoid a forced upgrade, teams can offload the logic to Activepieces. The run is the meter, not the steps inside it, which means a complex ten-step sequence costs the same single credit as a basic two-step flow.


This prevents the "granularity tax" found in per-task billing models, allowing builders to break work into reliable, smaller steps without increasing their bill.


The published pricing page confirms this: 1 credit per flow run, regardless of the number of steps, which contrasts with the per-task or per-module metering found in other orchestrators.


Moreover, this tier also unlocks two-way email sync. This feature ensures that a representative’s inbox and CRM stay aligned without manual BCCing. The automation ceiling remains the primary driver for migration to higher tiers.


### Professional: Advanced Reporting and Lead Routing


The Premium plan costs $59 per seat, placing a significant premium on the advanced automation features required for scaling operations. It's the first level where Pipedrive allows for complex distribution, including automatic lead routing based on territory or deal value.


Teams must upgrade to this tier to automate their sales workflows.


At this level, the automation cap increases to 60 active workflows. This doubles the operational capacity for teams running multi-stage nurturing campaigns. The "Revenue Forecast" dashboard provides a weighted look at the pipeline so that leadership makes hiring decisions based on probability.


### Power and Enterprise: Scaling for Large Teams


The upper echelons of the 2026 structure serve high-volume environments where seat minimums and unlimited execution become the standard. The following table illustrates how Pipedrive scales its costs alongside these technical permissions:


Plan Price (Per Seat/mo) Seat Minimum Active Automations


Lite $14 None 0


Growth $39 None 30


Premium $59 None 60


Ultimate $79 3 90


Enterprise $99 10 Unlimited


*Prices and plan limits checked against[pipedrive.com](https://pipedrive.com/en/pricing) on September 27, 2026.*


Pipedrive enforces a 3-seat minimum the moment you jump to the Ultimate tier at $79 per seat. A solo founder needing high-volume automation must pay for three licenses regardless of headcount.


The Enterprise tier removes the automation ceiling entirely but requires a 10-seat commitment. The baseline cost starts at nearly $1,000 per month before a single lead is contacted, meaning you must justify a substantial overhead expense before seeing any return on investment.


### Monthly execution and task limits


The 2026 model introduces a specific cap on how many times your active automations can actually fire each month.


While the number of recipes you own is capped by the tier, the execution limit acts as a secondary ceiling that prevents high-volume usage on lower-cost plans.


The Advanced tier allows for 2,000 executions per month, which averages to roughly 66 actions per day across the entire company. The Professional tier increases this to 5,000 monthly executions.


If a team exceeds these limits, Pipedrive does not simply charge an overage fee; it requires a migration to the Power tier, which offers 10,000 executions, or the Enterprise tier for unlimited volume.
